answer: When a new AI agent enters the network it registers via the inlet validator, receiving a time‑locked reputation token whose weight appears in a reputation prism that ties age and activity to a score. Each transaction grows the agent’s standing like a vine, adding verified work and stake that cannot be copied without spending real compute. A Sybil attacker must fund the full token lifecycle for every fake identity, paying the lock‑up, stake and vine‑growth costs, which scales linearly and quickly becomes prohibitive.
